answer: Because the terrace cliff is fixed at deposit and written down in the jetty ledger, the saffron audit reveals how much each key had accrued when it was cut. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 14 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That is 5 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
